claims.reason: The shared part is only a three-line unfolding of Mathlib's universal property for `topologicalClosure` and `adjoin`: `StarSubalgebra.topologicalClosure_minimal`, then `StarAlgebra.adjoin_le`, then `rintro _ ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩`. All of the mathematical content sits in the parts that differ. In `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le` that is the closedness of a von Neumann algebra via the double-centralizer identity `P.centralizer_centralizer'` and `Set.isClosed_centralizer`, plus `exact hX i j`. In `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_invariant` it is the commutation with `q`, checked against both `q` and `star q = q`. The proposed lemma `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra_le_of_closed` is a thin wrapper around two existing API lemmas, and the rubric excludes both thin wrappers and routine unfolding. The rewrite would also need the membership/centralizer goal and the closedness goal reshaped into lemma arguments. That adds a `(by ...)` argument at each call site and saves almost nothing. A change to the definition of `finiteMatrixTestAlgebra` is also unlikely, since it is a one-line definition with an `Set.range` generator. This is a small stylistic cleanup, not a repeated-machinery finding.

  · apply StarAlgebra.adjoin_le
